text:
maria: heads-up — i opened a draft PR for integrating FlashAttention v3 + v2 fallback into the kernel chooser. need quick feedback on the rollout plan and telemetry we should capture.
ankur: nice. link?
maria: <https://redwood.internal/ops/flashv3-integration|flashv3 integration draft> — key points: prefer v3 on short/medium sequences, fallback to v2 for paged-attn workloads and when kv-cache hits are high.
tj: curious — what perf deltas are we seeing in raw kernels? numbers please.
maria: from local perf runs on a8g: seq128 batch8: v3 = 11.2 ms, v2 = 14.6 ms (~1.3x). seq1024 batch2: v3 = 58 ms, v2 = 60 ms (~1.03x). seq8192 paged test: v3 regressed to 420 ms vs v2 310 ms. looks like memory access pattern + kernel tiling mismatch.
sophia: yikes on 8192. is that reproduced with KV cache enabled (serving path)?
maria: yes. with KV caching and frequent prefix reuse v3 sometimes triggers larger GPU memory pressure causing paging to host (we saw NVLink spills in perf traces).
perf-bot: profile summary (1769988000): 
```
cpu: small impact
gpu: v3 faster on dense blocks, regresses on long-seq paged access
mem: increased transient allocations with v3 paged path
```
ankur: so kernel chooser needs to be aware of: sequence length distribution, kv cache hit ratio, and a memory-pressure signal. also probably a per-model fflag map.
leo: we should avoid per-request heavy heuristics. better to compute routing decisions per-route (per-customer/model) and cache that decision for X minutes.
tj: agree. propose heuristics: if p95(seq_len) < 2048 -> prefer v3. if p95 > 4096 -> prefer v2. if kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6 and avg_prefix_len > 1024 -> prefer v2. if memory_headroom < 10% -> force-fallback v2.
maria: drafted a simple JSON config for the runtime chooser:
```
{
  "rules": [
    {"name": "short_seq_prefer_v3", "p95_seq_len_lt": 2048, "target_kernel": "flash_v3"},
    {"name": "long_seq_force_v2", "p95_seq_len_gt": 4096, "target_kernel": "flash_v2"},
    {"name": "kv_heavy_force_v2", "kv_hit_rate_gt": 0.6, "avg_prefix_gt": 1024, "target_kernel": "flash_v2"}
  ],
  "default": "flash_v3"
}
```
ankur: looks reasonable. add a ttl and manual override string on the rule so ops can flip quickly. also add a toggle to opt into fused-attention microbench path.
sophia: on telemetry — please emit: chosen_kernel, reason_code, p95_seq_len, kv_hit_rate, memory_headroom_pct, fallback_count. also track per-request latency delta when fallback occurs.
maria: added those metrics to the draft telemetry table. pulling them into the console will let us drive canary aborts.
perf-bot: suggestion: add a synthetic canary with mixed workloads (70% short, 20% medium, 10% long) and a pure-paged test lane. run for at least 2k requests/hour for 4 hours.
leo: rollout steps proposal:
1) feature flag ff_flashv3_routing = off by default.
2) enable ff for test tenancy and perf lab. run synthetic canary.
3) enable for 5% of traffic (routes selected by heuristics) and compare p50/p95 + cost.
4) monitor fallback_count and out-of-memory events; if fallback_count > 0.5% or OOMs increased -> rollback.
5) if stable for 48h, ramp to 50% then 100% with regional stagger.
tj: add a safety net: auto-fallback if request latency > baseline * 1.25 or GPU mem headroom < 5%.
maria: note on batching heuristics: v3 prefers slightly larger batch sizes to amortize kernel overhead but we cannot increase latency SLO. propose dynamic batch window where we allow batch growth up to +40% if p50_latency < target/2.
ankur: need to simulate live traffic traces to tune that. I'll generate a replay with kv-cache semantics.
sophia: also watch token generation variance — when streaming small token responses, batching can hurt tail. ensure we record token-level latency.
maria: PR has canary deploy knobs and per-model override + example rollout script. PTAL: <https://redwood.internal/pr/3321|PR 3321>.
deploy-bot: canary started for ff_flashv3_routing on test-lab at 1769990300 :rocket:
ankur: i'll kick off the synthetic canary after lunch and post results here.
leo: thanks — i'm adding the rollback playbook to oncall runbook and will include alert thresholds.
sophia: one more thing: add a metric for "kernel_switch_rate" (how often requests flip kernel mid-session) — we want to avoid oscillation.
maria: good call. added. planning follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 to review canary metrics. :calendar:
